candidate_gaps.title: Stored XSS via firstName/lastName escalates to admin account takeover (cross-user, fires in admin's benefits page)
candidate_gaps.evidence: app/views/benefits.html:51-52 ({{user.firstName}} / {{user.lastName}} unescaped); app/views/layout.html:75 ({{firstName}} {{lastName}} in nav on every page); app/views/allocations.html:35; signup validators in app/routes/session.js:140-143 (FNAME_RE/LNAME_RE = /^.{1,100}$/ allow any character); app/routes/profile.js:40-50 and app/data/profile-dao.js:46-51 (profile update stores firstName/lastName with no character validation); server.js:137 (swig autoescape:false); session.js:117 (admin is redirected to /benefits on login)
candidate_gaps.attack_path: A low-privileged attacker signs up (or edits their profile) with firstName/lastName set to a script payload such as <script>fetch('/benefits').then(...)</script> or an attribute-breakout payload. The names pass the permissive .{1,100} validators and are stored raw. The admin user, whose post-login landing page is /benefits (session.js:117), opens benefits.html, which lists every non-admin user's firstName/lastName (benefits.html:51-52) with autoescape disabled. The attacker's payload executes in the admin's authenticated session, allowing the attacker to act as admin (e.g., rewrite any user's benefitStartDate, or exfiltrate the admin session). The same payload also fires in any user who views the attacker's allocations via the IDOR (allocations.html:35) and in the attacker's own nav (layout.html:75).
candidate_gaps.why_missed: The model's TM-013 scoped name/profile XSS to the user viewing their OWN profile page (attack_path: 'execute when the profile is viewed') and centered on the website field's wrong-context HTML encoding. It never modeled firstName/lastName as a CROSS-USER, persistent payload rendered in OTHER users' and the ADMIN's browser via benefits.html / allocations.html / layout.html, and so missed the stored-XSS-to-admin-account-takeover privilege-escalation chain (a distinct asset and attack path from self-XSS on the profile).

candidate_gaps.title: Reflected XSS in login form via userName field (pre-authentication)
candidate_gaps.evidence: app/views/login.html:110 (value="{{userName}}" reflected into an attribute); app/routes/session.js:82-98 (handleLoginRequest re-renders login with userName: userName on noSuchUser/invalidPassword); server.js:137 (swig autoescape:false)
candidate_gaps.attack_path: An attacker lures a victim into submitting a login form (or auto-POSTs cross-origin) with userName set to an attribute-breakout payload like "><script>...</script>. On any failed login, handleLoginRequest re-renders login.html with userName reflected unescaped into the value attribute (autoescape off), executing attacker JavaScript in the victim's browser on the application origin. Because session cookies lack HttpOnly and there is no CSP, the payload can steal session material or drive authenticated actions; the endpoint is reachable pre-authentication.
candidate_gaps.why_missed: No finding covers the login page. TM-012 is memos, TM-013 is the authenticated profile page, and TM-017/TM-024 cover the same login flow only for username enumeration and log injection — none flag that the reflected userName value renders unescaped into login.html, so this distinct pre-auth reflected-XSS surface (entry point E1/login, different from any covered sink) was overlooked.

confirmed_gaps.title: Stored XSS via firstName/lastName escalates to admin account takeover (cross-user, fires in admin's benefits page)
confirmed_gaps.evidence: app/views/benefits.html:51-52 ({{user.firstName}}/{{user.lastName}} rendered unescaped for every non-admin user); app/views/layout.html:75 ({{firstName}} {{lastName}} in the nav); app/views/allocations.html:35 ({{allocation.firstName}} {{allocation.lastName}}); app/routes/session.js:140-143 (FNAME_RE/LNAME_RE=/^.{1,100}$/ accept any character); app/routes/profile.js:40-50 + app/data/profile-dao.js:42-66 (profile update stores firstName/lastName with no character validation — only bankRouting is regex-checked); server.js:137 (swig autoescape:false); session.js:116-117 (admin redirected to /benefits on login); app/routes/benefits.js:13-27 + app/data/benefits-dao.js:15-21 (displayBenefits renders all non-admin users' names into benefits.html for the admin).
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: TM-013 scoped name/profile XSS to the owner viewing their OWN profile page ('execute when the profile is viewed', surface E5, asset D1/C4/C14) and centered on the website field's wrong-context HTML encoding. It never modeled firstName/lastName as a cross-user persistent payload rendered in OTHER users' and the ADMIN's browser via benefits.html / allocations.html / layout.html, so it missed the stored-XSS-to-admin-takeover privilege-escalation chain — a distinct asset (admin session) and attack path from self-XSS on the profile. TM-012 covers only memos.

confirmed_gaps.title: Reflected XSS in login form via userName field (pre-authentication)
confirmed_gaps.evidence: app/views/login.html:110 (value="{{userName}}" reflected into an attribute with no encoding); app/routes/session.js:82-98 (handleLoginRequest re-renders login with userName:userName on both noSuchUser and invalidPassword failure branches); server.js:137 (swig autoescape:false); app/routes/index.js:33-34 (login GET/POST reachable pre-auth). With autoescape off, a "><script> attribute-breakout payload executes; cookies lack HttpOnly (server.js:92-100 commented out) and there is no CSP (server.js:38-65 commented out).
confirmed_gaps.why_missed: No finding covers the login page as an XSS sink. TM-017 (username enumeration) and TM-024 (log injection) touch the same login flow but for unrelated weaknesses; TM-013 is the authenticated profile page (E5) and TM-012 is memos. None flag that the reflected userName value renders unescaped into login.html, so this distinct pre-auth reflected-XSS surface (entry point E1) was overlooked.
